en: Sanjaya, on the sacred field of Kurukshetra, my sons and the sons of Pandu gathered, eager to fight. What did they do?
speaker: Dhritarashtra said

en: Seeing the Pandava army drawn up for battle, King Duryodhana went to his teacher Drona and spoke.
speaker: Sanjaya said

en: Look, teacher, at this mighty army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed by your own gifted student, the son of Drupada.
Here are heroes and great archers, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata and the great chariot-warrior Drupada;
Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaibya, the best of men;
the bold Yudhamanyu, the brave Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra and the sons of Draupadi, all of them great chariot-warriors.

sa: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
tr: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama
nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tānbravīmi te
en: Now hear, best of the twice-born, about the leading warriors on our side. I name the commanders of my army for you.
Yourself, Bhishma, Karna and Kripa, victorious in battle; Ashvatthama, Vikarna and the son of Somadatta.

sa: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः।
tr: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ
en: And many other heroes ready to give their lives for me, armed with many kinds of weapons, all skilled in war.
Our army, guarded by Bhishma, is beyond measure; theirs, guarded by Bhima, is limited. (Readings of this verse differ: some take it to mean the opposite.)
So all of you, holding your positions at every point of entry, must protect Bhishma above all.
Then Bhishma, the mighty grandsire and eldest of the Kurus, roared like a lion and blew his conch, filling Duryodhana with joy.
At once conches and kettledrums, cymbals, drums and horns blared together, and the sound was tremendous.
Then, standing in their great chariot yoked to white horses, Krishna and Arjuna blew their divine conches.
Krishna blew Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and Bhima, doer of fearsome deeds, blew his great conch Paundra.
King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
The king of Kashi, a supreme archer; Shikhandi, the great chariot-warrior; Dhrishtadyumna, Virata and the unconquered Satyaki;
Drupada, the sons of Draupadi and the mighty-armed son of Subhadra each blew their own conch, O lord of the earth.
That roar echoed through earth and sky and tore at the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.
Then, seeing Dhritarashtra's sons arrayed for battle and the weapons about to fly, Arjuna, whose banner bore Hanuman, lifted his bow
and spoke to Krishna. Arjuna said: Achyuta, draw my chariot up between the two armies,
speaker: Arjuna said

en: so that I can look at those who stand here eager to fight, and see whom I must face in this battle.
Let me see the men gathered here to fight, wanting to please the ill-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
Asked this by Arjuna, Krishna drove the finest of chariots between the two armies,
speaker: Sanjaya said

en: in front of Bhishma, Drona and all the kings of the earth, and said: Partha, see all these Kurus gathered here.
There Arjuna saw, standing in both armies, fathers and grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends,
fathers-in-law and well-wishers. Seeing all these kinsmen arrayed before him, Arjuna, son of Kunti,
was overcome by deep compassion and spoke in sorrow. Arjuna said: Krishna, seeing my own people eager to fight,
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति।
tr: sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati
en: my limbs give way, my mouth goes dry, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.

sa: न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
tr: na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ
en: The Gandiva slips from my hand and my skin is burning. I cannot stand steady; my mind is reeling.
I see evil omens, Keshava, and I see no good in killing my own kin in battle.

sa: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
tr: na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca
kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā
en: I do not want victory, Krishna, nor a kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is a kingdom to us, Govinda, or pleasure, or even life itself?

sa: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
tr: yeṣāmarthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca
ta ime'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃstyaktvā dhanāni ca
en: Those for whose sake we want a kingdom, enjoyment and pleasure stand here in battle, ready to give up their lives and their wealth:
teachers, fathers, sons and grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other kinsmen.

sa: अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
tr: api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte
en: I do not want to kill them, Madhusudana, even if they kill me; not for rule over the three worlds, let alone for this earth.
What joy could we have from killing the sons of Dhritarashtra, Janardana? Only sin would come to us from slaying these aggressors.

sa: स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
tr: svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
en: So it is not right for us to kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our own kinsmen. How could we be happy, Madhava, after killing our own people?
Even if they, their minds overcome by greed, see no wrong in destroying a family or in betraying friends,
why should we, who see clearly the evil of destroying a family, not learn to turn away from this sin, Janardana?
When a family is destroyed, its timeless traditions perish; and when tradition perishes, disorder overtakes the whole family.
When disorder prevails, Krishna, the women of the family are led astray, and from that comes the mixing of social orders.
That confusion drags the family and its destroyers down to hell, and their ancestors fall too, deprived of the offerings of food and water.
Through these wrongs of those who destroy families and cause the mixing of orders, the age-old duties of community and family are lost.
We have heard, Janardana, that people whose family traditions are destroyed live in hell for a long time.

sa: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्।
tr: aho bata mahatpāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam
en: Alas, how strange that we are set on committing a great sin, ready to kill our own kin out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.
It would be better for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, killed me in battle, unarmed and not fighting back.
Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna put aside his bow and arrows and sank down on the seat of the chariot, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
speaker: Sanjaya said
